subject: Hosted API rate card — anchor SKUs, overage caps, and committed tiers
messages:
From: Nora Patel <nora.p@skyline.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.p@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.d@redwood.ai>
Cc: Skyline AI Procurement <procurement@skyline.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API rate card and large-volume commitments

Hi Monica / Priyom,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're putting together a vendor shortlist for our next-gen inference layer and want to understand Redwood's hosted API economics for truly large volumes. High level: Skyline expects to ramp to ~1.5B tokens/month within 3 months and then to ~3.5–4B/month across the first year if performance and costs look good.

Can you send a baseline hosted rate card (per-1k-token price), and outline what committed monthly tiers you support (e.g., 250M, 500M, 1B+, etc.), the discount progression, and your overage pricing mechanics? A few additional asks:
- Do you offer true-up annual commitments vs month-to-month?
- Any onboarding or one-time credits for an enterprise trial?
- How do regional egress or multi-region routing charges factor in?

Procurement will need a ballpark quote they can take into budget (can be redacted). We can share an expected ramp profile if that helps.

Best,
Nora
Nora Patel
Head of AI Ops, Skyline AI
N: +1 (415) 555-0192
From: Monica Patel <monica.p@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Patel <nora.p@skyline.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.d@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.c@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API rate card and large-volume commitments

Hi Nora — great to hear and thanks for the details. Attaching our Q2 rate card for hosted API (pdf) and a short SKU request template. Below is an abbreviated summary to get the conversation moving; attaching a simple model for your ramp as well.

Baseline (list) hosted generation price: $0.0040 per 1k tokens
Embedding price (if relevant): $0.020 per 1k tokens

Committed-tier discounts (examples):
- 0–250M tokens/month: no discount (list)
- 250M–500M: 10% off list
- 500M–1B: 15% off list
- 1B–2B: 18% off list
- 2B+: 22% off list

Overage mechanics: overages billed at list price with the committed discount applied; monthly true-up is allowed. We commonly offer an annualized committed contract (12 months) with staged true-ups at quarter boundaries for customers planning multi-quarter ramp.

Pilot / onboarding credits: we typically offer a one-time onboarding credit sized to the initial committed bucket for enterprise pilots (example: a 3-month pilot at 200M/month could be supported with a $25k credit).

Notes / caveats:
- Regional egress: outbound data egress to non-US regions can incur cloud provider egress; Redwood does not add a separate surcharge for multi-region routing, but we will call out cloud egress in the invoice if applicable.
- Custom discounts above 2B tokens/month are evaluated with finance; some customers get bespoke slab pricing and overage caps.

Next steps: if you can confirm a target committed bucket and preferred contract length, I can prepare an initial commercial proposal and loop in Ben (pricing) + Priyom (solutions) for technical constraints.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Hosted_RateCard_Q2_2027.pdf, Skyline_SKU_Request_Form.xlsx
From: Nora Patel <nora.p@skyline.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.p@redwood.ai>
Cc: Skyline AI Procurement <procurement@skyline.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.d@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 08:56:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API rate card and large-volume commitments

Monica — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. A few follow-ups after reviewing with procurement:

1) Discount profile: Our preference is a flatter, higher discount once we cross 1B/month. Instead of stepped bands, procurement prefers a single negotiated discount applied to all consumption once the committed threshold is hit. For procurement modeling we asked for ~20–22% across the board if we commit to 1B tokens/month for 12 months.

2) Overage cap: we need a maximum cap on overage billing (e.g., overage billed at no more than 1.1x the discounted rate for three months while we stabilize).

3) Billing cadence & true-up: we prefer monthly billing with quarterly true-up and a single annual reconciliation.

4) Security evidence: procurement also asked to attach SOC 2 Type II report or an attestation link alongside the quote. Can you include that?

5) Regional question: We will operate across US + EU regions. Please confirm there are no per-request regional routing fees and provide an example invoice line for egress that procurement can include in their model.

If you can send an updated commercial term sheet with the above options (pilot credit, a 1B committed bucket option, and the overage cap), we can fast-follow our internal approvals.

Best,
Nora
From: Monica Patel <monica.p@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.c@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.d@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.b@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Skyline ask — propose approval for custom 1B commit concession

Team — short summary and recommended concession for Skyline (they're in final vendor comparisons):

Customer ask (from thread):
- 1B tokens/month committed for 12 months (monthly billing + quarterly true-up)
- Flat 20–22% discount applied to all consumption when commitment is active
- Overage cap <= 1.1x discounted rate for first 3 months post-ramp
- One-time onboarding credit requested ($50k suggested by procurement)
- SOC 2 attestation and sample invoice line for US+EU egress

Commercial recommendation (proposed by me):
- Offer 1B tokens/month committed for 12 months at 20% off list
- Cap overage at 1.1x the discounted per-1k rate for the first 90 days after ramp; revert to standard overage thereafter
- One-time onboarding credit: $50,000 (applied against first invoice)
- Provide SOC 2 Type II link and example egress invoice lines (finance to confirm wording)

Rationale: the concession is within our precedent bands for large customers, protects Skyline during ramp, and locks a predictable ARR profile. We can gate the onboarding credit on a signed SOW + initial payment milestone.

Ask: Ben — please confirm finance approves the 20% flat discount + $50k credit. Priyom — confirm any technical limitations with honoring multi-region routing for their EU usage and whether we need to call out extra costs. Lauren — I may need a short commercial term sheet and an updated quote PDF (internal_custom_quote_SKY-4621.pdf) if finance approves.

Thanks — if we greenlight, I'll send the draft term sheet to Nora and procurement.

— Monica
